readmeExcerpt:
CLAURST

Agentic Coding for Builders who Ship


--- Claurst is an **open-source, multi-provider terminal coding agent** built from the ground up in Rust. It started as a clean-room reimplementation of Claude Code's behavior (from [spec](https://github.com/kuberwastaken/claurst/tree/main/spec)) and has since evolved into an amazing TUI pair programmer with multi-provider support, a rich UI, plugin system, a companion named Rustle, chat forking, memory consolidation, and much more. It's fast, it's memory-efficient, it's yours to run however you want, and there's no tracking or telemetry. --- > [!IMPORTANT] > **Claurst is now officially in Beta (v0.2.0).** The core agent, multi-provider routing, and TUI are stable enough for daily driving — expect rough edges around experimental features (flagged below). Bug reports and PRs welcome. > [!NOTE] > **Recent Updates (v0.2.0, see the [changelog](docs/changelog.md)):** > > - **Sandbox and permissions:** on macOS, Bash commands run in a Seatbelt sandbox that limits writes to the workspace and blocks network by default (`/sandbox-toggle`). Bash approvals are matched per command, approvals can be saved for the current project, and `--allowed-tools` / `--disallowed-tools` are enforced. See [Permission rules](docs/configuration.md#permission-rules-and-approvals) and [Shell Sandbox](docs/configuration.md#shell-sandbox). > > - **Hooks:** Claude Code's hooks contract (settings shape, events, JSON stdin/stdout, exit code 2, timeouts), including plugin hooks. See [Hooks](docs/hooks.md). > > - **Skills and instruction files:** `AGENTS.md` and `CLAUDE.md` files are loaded from the git root down to the working directory, with `@include`; skills from `.claurst/skills`, `.agents/skills` and `.claude/skills` are listed to the model. See [Instruction files](docs/configuration.md#instruction-files-agentsmd--claudemd) and [Skills](docs/configuration.md#skills). > > - **Headless runs:** typed `stream-json` events, documented exit codes, `--resume` / `--continue`, and `--json-schema` for a structured answer. See [Headless mode](docs/advanced.md#headless-mode). > > - **Providers:** Anthropic prompt caching and adaptive thinking; ChatGPT (Codex) subscription token refresh, prompt caching and reasoning replay; one retry policy and context compaction for every provider. > > - **/share support:** Use `/share` to share chat sessions with others via unlisted GitHub Gists. `[EXPERIMENTAL]` > > - **Free Mode:** Try out Free in '/connect' to get a great agentic coding experience in Claurst for absolutely free (or as good as free gets you :P). `[EXPERIMENTAL]` > > - **/goal support:** Try out `/goal ` to see claurst keep working an objective, spanning multiple turns instead of stopping after one normal turn. `[EXPERIMENTAL]` > > - **ultracode:** The **highest effort level** — pick it in the effort selector (`/effort`, where it sits past `max` on the "Smarter" end with an animated purple spectrum) or just type **`ultracode`** anywhere in your prompt. The keyword lights up with a purple gradient (claurst's take on Claude Code's `ultrathink`) and that turn runs at the model's top reasoning **plus** a disciplined plan → delegate → integrate → verify workflow that fans bounded packets out across native subagents (`Agent`), swarms (`TeamCreate`), and background tasks (`TaskCreate`). Composes with `/goal` for sustained multi-turn objectives. `[EXPERIMENTAL]` --- # Getting Started ## Quick install (one-liner) **Linux / macOS:** ```bash curl -fsSL https://github.com/kuberwastaken/claurst/releases/latest/download/install.sh | bash ``` **Windows (PowerShell):** ```powershell irm https://github.com/kuberwastaken/claurst/releases/latest/download/install.ps1 | iex ``` This drops `claurst` into `~/.local/bin` (or `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Programs\claurst` on Windows; Git Bash uses the same Windows path) and adds it to your `PATH` automatically. Open a new terminal and run `claurst`. ## Via npm / bun If you have Node.js or Bun installed, you can install Claurst as a global package. The postinstall script automatically downloads the right pre-built binary for your platform. ```bash # npm npm install -g claurst # bun bun install -g claurst # or run without installing npx claurst bunx claurst ``` To upgrade later, run: ```bash claurst upgrade ``` > Pin a specific version with `--version 0.1.0` on either installer, or `claurst upgrade --version 0.1.0`. ## Manual download If you'd rather grab the binary yourself, the latest archives are on [**GitHub Releases**](https://github.com/kuberwastaken/claurst/releases): | Platform | Archive | |----------|---------| | **Windows** x86_64 | `claurst-windows-x86_64.zip` | | **Linux** x86_64 | `claurst-linux-x86_64.tar.gz` | | **Linux** aarch64 | `claurst-linux-aarch64.tar.gz` | | **macOS** Intel | `claurst-macos-x86_64.tar.gz` | | **macOS** Apple Silicon | `claurst-macos-aarch64.tar.gz` | Each archive contains a single `claurst` (or `claurst.exe`) binary. Extract it and put it on your `PATH`. ## Build from source ```bash git clone https://github.com/kuberwastaken/claurst.git cd claurst/src-rust cargo build --release --package claurst # Binary is at target/release/claurst ``` **Raspberry Pi / systems without ALSA** (e.g. Debian Trixie, headless servers): ```bash # Build without voice/microphone support — no libasound2-dev required cargo build --release --package claurst --no-default-features ``` ## First run ```bash # Set your API key (or use /connect inside Claurst to configure) export ANTHROPIC_API_KEY=sk-ant-... # Or sign in with a ChatGPT subscription (Codex) claurst codex login # Start Claurst claurst # Or run a one-shot headless query claurst -p "explain this codebase" # Headless with one JSON event per line, or a structured answer claurst -p --output-format stream-json "fix the failing test" claurst -p --output-format json --json-schema schema.json "is this branch ready to merge?" ``` Claurst asks before running commands and editing files; see [Permission modes](docs/configuration.md#permission-modes). Project instructions go in `AGENTS.md` or `CLAUDE.md` at the repository root. ## Devcontainer setup After cloning this repository, open it in VS Code and use Reopen in Container to start the development environment. Prerequisites: - Docker installed on your host machine: https://www.docker.com/products/docker-desktop/ GPG and SSH forwarding is enabled in the devcontainer, given you have it set up on your host machine. Follow [this guide](https://code.visualstudio.com/remote/advancedcontainers/sharing-git-credentials) if you need help with that. ### Devcontainer features - Base image: `rust:1-bullseye`. - Preinstalled build dependencies: `gnupg2`, `libasound2-dev`, `libxdo-dev`, and `pkg-config`. - Devcontainer features enabled: `common-utils` (with `vscode` user `uid/gid 1000` and Zsh install disabled), `git`, and `docker-outside-of-docker` (`moby: false`). - Runs as `vscode` user by default. - Persistent Cargo caches via named volumes for `/usr/local/cargo/registry` and `/usr/local/cargo/git`. - Binds local `.claurst` into `/home/vscode/.claurst` for local settings/session history access. - Sets `GNUPGHOME=/home/vscode/.gnupg` and prepends `src-rust/target/debug` and `src-rust/target/release` to `PATH`. - Post-create setup creates and permissions `.gnupg`, and fixes ownership for `/usr/local/cargo`. - VS Code setting `terminal.integrated.inheritEnv` is enabled. ## Editor integration (Agent Client Protocol) Claurst speaks the [**Agent Client Protocol (ACP)**](https://agentclientprotocol.com) — the open protocol pioneered by Zed for editor-to-agent communication. Any ACP-compatible editor (Zed, Neovim, JetBrains plugins, …) can drive Claurst as a subprocess and present it in the editor's native chat UI. To use Claurst as the agent in your editor, point its ACP integration at: ``` command: claurst args: ["acp"] ``` **Zed example** (`~/.config/zed/settings.json`): ```jsonc { "agent_servers": { "claurst": { "command": "claurst", "args": ["acp"] } } } ``` Claurst will run in JSON-RPC 2.0 mode over stdio. It implements `initialize`, `session/new`, `session/prompt`, and `session/cancel`, streams `session/update` notifications (text deltas, agent thinking, tool calls with their progress + results), and evaluates tool permissions with the same rules as the TUI, sending only the calls that need approval to `session/request_permission` so the editor can show a native approval dialog. Each session uses the settings, instruction files and trusted MCP servers of its working directory. Configure your provider / API key in `~/.claurst/settings.json` (or `claurst auth login`, `claurst codex login`, or `/connect` inside the TUI) before launching — the ACP agent uses the same credentials and providers as the interactive TUI. Enable verbose ACP logging (to stderr — never stdout, which would corrupt the protocol) by setting `CLAURST_ACP_LOG=debug`. ### Listing on the ACP Registry The [Agent Client Protocol registry](https://github.com/agentclientprotocol/registry) is the canonical directory editors look up when offering "available agents". To get Claurst listed: 1. Fork [`agentclientprotocol/registry`](https://github.com/agentclientprotocol/registry). 2. Create a `claurst/` folder at the repo root and drop in the prepared manifest from this repo: [`src-rust/crates/acp/registry-template/agent.json`](src-rust/crates/acp/registry-template/agent.json). Bump the `version` and release-archive URLs to match the latest GitHub release. 3. Add `claurst/icon.svg` (16×16 recommended) — the Rustle logo from [`public/`](public/) is a fine starting point. 4. Open a PR to the registry. The registry CI validates `agent.json` against [the schema](https://github.com/agentclientprotocol/registry/blob/main/agent.schema.json) before merge. After merge, Zed and other ACP-aware editors will pick up Claurst on their next registry refresh. ## Documentation For more info on how to configure Claurst, [head over to our docs](https://claurst.kuber.studio/docs). >**PS:** The original breakdown of the findings from Claude Code's source that started this project is on [my blog](https://kuber.studio/blog/AI/Claude-Code's-Entire-Source-Code-Got-Leaked-via-a-Sourcemap-in-npm,-Let's-Talk-About-it) - the full technical writeup of what was found, how the leak happened, and what it revealed. --- ## Contributing Claurst is built for the community, by the community and we'd love your help making it better. readmeHtml:
CLAURST

Agentic Coding for Builders who Ship


Claurst is an open-source, multi-provider terminal coding agent built from the ground up in Rust. It started as a clean-room reimplementation of Claude Code's behavior (from spec) and has since evolved into an amazing TUI pair programmer with multi-provider support, a rich UI, plugin system, a companion named Rustle, chat forking, memory consolidation, and much more.

It's fast, it's memory-efficient, it's yours to run however you want, and there's no tracking or telemetry.

Important

Claurst is now officially in Beta (v0.2.0). The core agent, multi-provider routing, and TUI are stable enough for daily driving — expect rough edges around experimental features (flagged below). Bug reports and PRs welcome.

Note

Recent Updates (v0.2.0, see the changelog):

  • Sandbox and permissions: on macOS, Bash commands run in a Seatbelt sandbox that limits writes to the workspace and blocks network by default (/sandbox-toggle). Bash approvals are matched per command, approvals can be saved for the current project, and --allowed-tools / --disallowed-tools are enforced. See Permission rules and Shell Sandbox.

  • Hooks: Claude Code's hooks contract (settings shape, events, JSON stdin/stdout, exit code 2, timeouts), including plugin hooks. See Hooks.

  • Skills and instruction files: AGENTS.md and CLAUDE.md files are loaded from the git root down to the working directory, with @include; skills from .claurst/skills, .agents/skills and .claude/skills are listed to the model. See Instruction files and Skills.

  • Headless runs: typed stream-json events, documented exit codes, --resume / --continue, and --json-schema for a structured answer. See Headless mode.

  • Providers: Anthropic prompt caching and adaptive thinking; ChatGPT (Codex) subscription token refresh, prompt caching and reasoning replay; one retry policy and context compaction for every provider.

  • /share support: Use /share to share chat sessions with others via unlisted GitHub Gists. [EXPERIMENTAL]

  • Free Mode: Try out Free in '/connect' to get a great agentic coding experience in Claurst for absolutely free (or as good as free gets you :P). [EXPERIMENTAL]

  • /goal support: Try out /goal <objective> to see claurst keep working an objective, spanning multiple turns instead of stopping after one normal turn. [EXPERIMENTAL]

  • ultracode: The highest effort level — pick it in the effort selector (/effort, where it sits past max on the "Smarter" end with an animated purple spectrum) or just type ultracode anywhere in your prompt. The keyword lights up with a purple gradient (claurst's take on Claude Code's ultrathink) and that turn runs at the model's top reasoning plus a disciplined plan → delegate → integrate → verify workflow that fans bounded packets out across native subagents (Agent), swarms (TeamCreate), and background tasks (TaskCreate). Composes with /goal for sustained multi-turn objectives. [EXPERIMENTAL]

Getting Started

Quick install (one-liner)

Linux / macOS:

curl -fsSL https://github.com/kuberwastaken/claurst/releases/latest/download/install.sh | bash

Windows (PowerShell):

irm https://github.com/kuberwastaken/claurst/releases/latest/download/install.ps1 | iex

This drops claurst into ~/.local/bin (or %LOCALAPPDATA%\Programs\claurst on Windows; Git Bash uses the same Windows path) and adds it to your PATH automatically. Open a new terminal and run claurst.

Via npm / bun

If you have Node.js or Bun installed, you can install Claurst as a global package. The postinstall script automatically downloads the right pre-built binary for your platform.

# npm
npm install -g claurst

# bun
bun install -g claurst

# or run without installing
npx claurst
bunx claurst

To upgrade later, run:

claurst upgrade

Pin a specific version with --version 0.1.0 on either installer, or claurst upgrade --version 0.1.0.

Manual download

If you'd rather grab the binary yourself, the latest archives are on GitHub Releases:

Platform Archive
Windows x86_64 claurst-windows-x86_64.zip
Linux x86_64 claurst-linux-x86_64.tar.gz
Linux aarch64 claurst-linux-aarch64.tar.gz
macOS Intel claurst-macos-x86_64.tar.gz
macOS Apple Silicon claurst-macos-aarch64.tar.gz

Each archive contains a single claurst (or claurst.exe) binary. Extract it and put it on your PATH.

Build from source

git clone https://github.com/kuberwastaken/claurst.git
cd claurst/src-rust
cargo build --release --package claurst

# Binary is at target/release/claurst

Raspberry Pi / systems without ALSA (e.g. Debian Trixie, headless servers):

# Build without voice/microphone support — no libasound2-dev required
cargo build --release --package claurst --no-default-features

First run

# Set your API key (or use /connect inside Claurst to configure)
export ANTHROPIC_API_KEY=sk-ant-...

# Or sign in with a ChatGPT subscription (Codex)
claurst codex login

# Start Claurst
claurst

# Or run a one-shot headless query
claurst -p "explain this codebase"

# Headless with one JSON event per line, or a structured answer
claurst -p --output-format stream-json "fix the failing test"
claurst -p --output-format json --json-schema schema.json "is this branch ready to merge?"

Claurst asks before running commands and editing files; see Permission modes. Project instructions go in AGENTS.md or CLAUDE.md at the repository root.

Devcontainer setup

After cloning this repository, open it in VS Code and use Reopen in Container to start the development environment.

Prerequisites:

  • Docker installed on your host machine: https://www.docker.com/products/docker-desktop/

GPG and SSH forwarding is enabled in the devcontainer, given you have it set up on your host machine. Follow this guide if you need help with that.

Devcontainer features

  • Base image: rust:1-bullseye.
  • Preinstalled build dependencies: gnupg2, libasound2-dev, libxdo-dev, and pkg-config.
  • Devcontainer features enabled: common-utils (with vscode user uid/gid 1000 and Zsh install disabled), git, and docker-outside-of-docker (moby: false).
  • Runs as vscode user by default.
  • Persistent Cargo caches via named volumes for /usr/local/cargo/registry and /usr/local/cargo/git.
  • Binds local .claurst into /home/vscode/.claurst for local settings/session history access.
  • Sets GNUPGHOME=/home/vscode/.gnupg and prepends src-rust/target/debug and src-rust/target/release to PATH.
  • Post-create setup creates and permissions .gnupg, and fixes ownership for /usr/local/cargo.
  • VS Code setting terminal.integrated.inheritEnv is enabled.

Editor integration (Agent Client Protocol)

Claurst speaks the Agent Client Protocol (ACP) — the open protocol pioneered by Zed for editor-to-agent communication. Any ACP-compatible editor (Zed, Neovim, JetBrains plugins, …) can drive Claurst as a subprocess and present it in the editor's native chat UI.

To use Claurst as the agent in your editor, point its ACP integration at:

command: claurst
args:    ["acp"]

Zed example (~/.config/zed/settings.json):

{
  "agent_servers": {
    "claurst": {
      "command": "claurst",
      "args": ["acp"]
    }
  }
}

Claurst will run in JSON-RPC 2.0 mode over stdio. It implements initialize, session/new, session/prompt, and session/cancel, streams session/update notifications (text deltas, agent thinking, tool calls with their progress + results), and evaluates tool permissions with the same rules as the TUI, sending only the calls that need approval to session/request_permission so the editor can show a native approval dialog. Each session uses the settings, instruction files and trusted MCP servers of its working directory.

Configure your provider / API key in ~/.claurst/settings.json (or claurst auth login, claurst codex login, or /connect inside the TUI) before launching — the ACP agent uses the same credentials and providers as the interactive TUI.

Enable verbose ACP logging (to stderr — never stdout, which would corrupt the protocol) by setting CLAURST_ACP_LOG=debug.

Listing on the ACP Registry

The Agent Client Protocol registry is the canonical directory editors look up when offering "available agents". To get Claurst listed:

  1. Fork agentclientprotocol/registry.
  2. Create a claurst/ folder at the repo root and drop in the prepared manifest from this repo: src-rust/crates/acp/registry-template/agent.json. Bump the version and release-archive URLs to match the latest GitHub release.
  3. Add claurst/icon.svg (16×16 recommended) — the Rustle logo from public/ is a fine starting point.
  4. Open a PR to the registry. The registry CI validates agent.json against the schema before merge.

After merge, Zed and other ACP-aware editors will pick up Claurst on their next registry refresh.

Documentation

For more info on how to configure Claurst, head over to our docs.

PS: The original breakdown of the findings from Claude Code's source that started this project is on my blog - the full technical writeup of what was found, how the leak happened, and what it revealed.

Contributing

Claurst is built for the community, by the community and we'd love your help making it better. Please see and include AGENTS.md for project-specific rules (for both humans and agents).

Open an issue for bugs, ideas, or questions, or Raise a PR to fix bugs, add features, or improve documentation.

Important Notice

This repository does not hold a copy of the proprietary Claude Code TypeScript source code. This is a clean-room Rust reimplementation of Claude Code's behavior.

The process was explicitly two-phase:

Specification spec/ — An AI agent analyzed the source and produced exhaustive behavioral specifications and improvements, deviated from the original: architecture, data flows, tool contracts, system designs. No source code was carried forward.

Implementation src-rust/ — A separate AI agent implemented from the spec alone, never referencing the original TypeScript. The output is idiomatic Rust that reproduces the behavior, not the expression.

This mirrors the legal precedent established by Phoenix Technologies v. IBM (1984) — clean-room engineering of the BIOS — and the principle from Baker v. Selden (1879) that copyright protects expression, not ideas or behavior.

releases.name: Claurst v0.2.0
releases.body:
Parity release. Deep-dives against pi, Codex CLI and OpenCode found that much of the documented surface was inert; v0.2.0 makes it real and closes the gaps. Full details per area in [docs/changelog.md](https://github.com/Kuberwastaken/claurst/blob/main/docs/changelog.md).


## Breaking
- MCP tools are exposed as `mcp__<server>__<tool>`; update allow/deny rules and hook matchers that named the old form (#463)
- Hooks use the Claude Code contract: matchers, JSON on stdin/stdout, exit codes and timeouts; the old hooks config shape is not read (#483)
- Permission rules for Bash match per command, so `Bash(git *)` style rules apply to each command in a pipeline, not the whole line (#469)
- Project `.claurst/commands` is no longer read; commands come from skills and instruction files (#474)
- Headless: stream-json events are typed, exit codes are defined, and `--max-turns` defaults to 100 (#481)
- macOS: the Bash sandbox is on by default with network off; use `/sandbox-toggle network on` or the retry-unsandboxed prompt (#476)
- Deny rules apply in every mode, including bypass; ApplyPatch is checked as Edit, so rules naming ApplyPatch no longer match (#469, #477)
- ACP failed turns return

aiSummary.oneLiner: A highly performant, open-source terminal coding agent built in Rust with multi-provider LLM support.
aiSummary.whatItDoes: Claurst is a fast and memory-efficient multi-provider terminal coding agent engineered entirely in Rust. Originally conceived as a clean-room implementation of Claude Code, it has evolved into a fully-featured TUI pair programmer that operates securely without telemetry. It provides developers with an intelligent companion, Rustle, and supports advanced features like chat forking, memory consolidation, and a robust plugin ecosystem. By natively executing terminal commands and integrating deeply with the local filesystem, it allows developers to architect, debug, and ship code autonomously directly from their command line.
keyFeatures: Rust-based performance: Delivers exceptional speed and minimal memory footprint by being built natively in Rust.
Multi-provider routing: Seamlessly connects to various LLM providers, allowing users to choose their preferred model for coding tasks.
Terminal User Interface (TUI): Provides a rich, interactive console environment for paired programming and task management.
Privacy-first architecture: Operates entirely locally without any tracking, telemetry, or forced cloud dependencies.
Advanced chat management: Supports chat forking and memory consolidation to maintain context across complex coding sessions.
Extensible plugin system: Allows developers to extend the agent's capabilities with custom tools and workflows.

useCases.title: Terminal-based pair programming
useCases.description: Developers use the TUI to collaboratively write, refactor, and debug code directly within their terminal environment.

useCases.title: Privacy-sensitive codebase analysis
useCases.description: Enterprise engineers analyze proprietary code without telemetry, ensuring source code never leaves their controlled environment.

useCases.title: Multi-model coding assistance
useCases.description: Users switch between different LLM providers based on the complexity of the task, optimizing for speed or reasoning capability.

useCases.title: Complex session management
useCases.description: Architects use chat forking to explore multiple implementation paths simultaneously without losing the original context.

aiSummary.whoIsItFor: Claurst is tailored for developers, system administrators, and privacy-conscious engineers who prefer terminal-based workflows. It is ideal for those who want a highly performant, customizable coding assistant without relying on proprietary, telemetry-heavy tools.
